industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, because the industry is split and the sector rows carry the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Chris Wood (via Jefferies, 17 Oct) would diversify from artificial intelligence into healthcare and financials, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, C prior at industry level, with Medtech capital goods at A; but pharmaceuticals against medical technology was not spoken to by any source, clinical-stage biotech is the unproven, cash-burning end the Fragility axis punishes (B.11 at D, relative strength F), and only five of the 149 Pool stocks are healthcare. Pharma/biotech and Hospitals carry B. Counter-case for B at the industry: 94 stocks, the second largest industry, and a defensive rotation that is now five weeks old; for D: a crowded destination.

sector.why: Neutral. Relative strength F both readings; no line in Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent) specific to distribution. No tilt.

geography.why: Underweight, carried unchanged with the reason strengthened. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the spillover from France to Italy is the new fact this week (Goldman, 16 Oct, 'tentative spillover to Italy'), and the Italian listings in the Pool are bank-heavy (Monte dei Paschi, Credito Emiliano, Mediobanca) beside global businesses (Eni, Saipem, Tenaris, STMicroelectronics, Technoprobe, Reply). Not Double Underweight because Goldman also says contagion risk is lower than in 2011-15, its fragmentation index shows risk 'remains limited', and Southern European banks are healthier; relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to F if the fragmentation index rises or the Italian premium is read above 150 basis points; back to C under 100.
